title: [v0.92.1][AWS-B] AWS access and billing baseline
body:
## Outcome

Produce one accepted AWS access and billing control baseline.

## Primary deliverable

One accepted AWS access and billing baseline with independently recoverable corporate administration, governed Agent Toolkit access, and visible cost controls.

## Verification result

Root recovery, human and workload access, Agent Toolkit configuration, agent-specific IAM guardrails, CloudWatch and CloudTrail activity visibility, billing, budget, anomaly, export, and cost-attribution readbacks pass without removing the proven administrator path.

## Unit boundary

Issue completion is exactly one accepted access-and-billing baseline; individual readbacks are evidence inputs and do not close independently.

## Dependencies

- AWS-A: #484

## Retained predecessor scope

- None; this is new v0.92.1 work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Corporate recovery does not depend on one personal factor
- [ ] Human workload and agent-initiated identities are distinguishable
- [ ] Agent Toolkit for AWS is configured for the approved Codex path with AWS CLI 2.35 or newer
- [ ] IAM context policies bind agent actions with read-only default posture
- [ ] CloudWatch metrics and CloudTrail requests are attributable
- [ ] Billing and budget ownership is visible
- [ ] Existing administrator access remains until replacement is proven

## Owned paths

- `infra/aws/account-foundation/**`
- `docs/operations/cloud/aws/access-billing/**`
- `docs/milestones/v0.92.1/evidence/cloud/aws-b/**`

## PVF lanes

- `root-recovery`
- `identity-census`
- `agent-toolkit-configuration`
- `agent-iam-guardrails`
- `agent-activity-audit`
- `billing-readback`
- `budget-and-anomaly`
- `credential-redaction`

## Stop conditions

- Replacement access is unproven
- Billing target is ambiguous
- Credentials would enter evidence

## Non-goals

- Organizations rollout
- Workload deployment
- Unrestricted agent mutation
- Removing break-glass access
